narr: A strong storm system led to significant impacts. Heavy rainfall amounts of 3 to 4.5 inches produced areas of flash flooding, with numerous road closures. The heavy rain drove the Ohio River above flood stage at Uniontown. Very strong wind gusts occurred, ranging between 50 and about 70 mph. These were associated with both thunderstorms and gradient winds afterwards. The line of storms moved through during the late morning and early afternoon, and then very strong gradient winds continued for several hours afterwards through the afternoon. An indirect fatality occurred the following day during cleanup operations. A 69-year-old man in Calloway County was killed when a large branch landed on him while he was cutting up the tree. The magnitude and duration of this wind produced significant damage to trees, power lines, and other outdoor property such as fences. Soggy ground due to the excessive rainfall likely contributed to some trees being more susceptible to being blown over. Numerous power outages occurred, some lasting into the following day. Six tornadoes occurred along the line of thunderstorms across western Kentucky. The strongest was rated EF-2 just south of Paducah. Finally, the lowest barometric pressure of all-time was observed in Paducah (977.7 mb). The center of the record strong low pressure system tracked from the bootheel of extreme southeast Missouri northeast right along the Ohio River. Very strong southwest winds occurred on the back side of the low pressure system in the afternoon. Gusts were up to around 60 mph. A semi was blown over on Interstate 24 in Trigg County.
ev: Kentucky Highway 80 West was closed at the 2.8 mile marker in Arlington, just west of U.S. Highway 51. Kentucky Highway 307 was closed near the 7 mile marker, between Kentucky 121 and U.S. Highway 62 due to flooding.

Flash flooding closed several roads in McCracken County. Kentucky 1255 was closed at the 1 to 2 mile marker, just west of the Kentucky 450 intersection. Kentucky 994 was closed at the 5.5 to 5.7 mile markers at the Kentucky 1410 intersection, due to flooding of Champion Creek. Kentucky 1410 was closed near Champion Creek from the 3.2 to 3.7 mile marker.

Harris Fork Creek was overflowing and flooding downtown Fulton. Kentucky Highway 94 was closed from the 7 to 11 mile markers in the lower bottomlands between Kentucky 311 and Kentucky 1099 due to water over the road.
U.S. Highway 62 experienced localized flooding between Calvert City and Possum Trot. Some side roads were covered.
Kentucky Route 1949 was closed at the 7 to 9 mile marker near the I-69 tunnel.
U.S. Highway 62 was closed at the Carlisle County line, where Mayfield Creek flows under the roadway.
U.S. Highway 51 was closed north and south of Clinton due to flooding. Kentucky Highway 307 was closed at the 13 to 14 mile markers. Kentucky 58 was closed at the 7 to 8 mile markers due to flooding.
Water was running across the road in places.

Flooding was curb deep in the city of Henderson on Green River Road among other streets. Four miles south-southeast of Henderson, water was covering part of the roadway on U.S. Highway 41 South at Smith Staples Road.

Several state roads were closed due to high water in Webster County, including Highways 132, 270, 138, and 2836. A few other state roads were open but covered with water. Some county roads were also affected by flooding.

A few state highways were closed due to high water, including Highways 760, 132, and 138. The westbound lane of U.S. Highway 60 was closed at the 8 mile marker. Some county roads were also affected by high water.
